pageInfo.subtitle: Master the advanced two-handed technique that extends your fretboard range and creates lightning-fast legato passages with unique tonal characteristics.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Tapping is an advanced guitar technique that uses both hands on the fretboard to create rapid legato passages, extended range arpeggios, and unique musical textures impossible to achieve through conventional picking. By using the right hand to "tap" notes on the fretboard while the left hand continues to fret normally, guitarists can play complex polyphonic passages, wide interval jumps, and create the signature sound of virtuoso rock, metal, and progressive music.

items.text: Use index or middle finger for tapping
Strike strings with firm, quick motion
Pull off cleanly to sound lower notes
Maintain consistent finger angle and pressure
Use proper finger placement and pressure

exercises.title: Basic One-Handed Tapping
exercises.description: Start with simple three-note patterns using one tapped note and two fretted notes. This establishes the basic tap-pull-hammer motion that forms the foundation of all tapping.

patternNote.text: Pattern: Tap high note -> Pull-off -> Hammer-on

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use your right hand index finger to tap the 12th fret firmly, then pull off to sound the 5th fret note, then hammer on to the 8th fret. Keep the motion fluid and even.

exercises.title: Ascending Tapping Sequences
exercises.description: Extend the basic pattern into ascending sequences that cover more range and create melodic lines that would be impossible with conventional picking techniques.

patternNote.text: Focus: Smooth position changes and consistent tapping pressure

notation.title: Ascending Three-Note Groups with Position Changes

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Practice each three-note group slowly before linking them together. Focus on smooth hand position changes and maintaining even volume across all notes.

exercises.title: Cross-String Tapping
exercises.description: Apply tapping across multiple strings to create wider interval patterns and more complex melodic lines that span the guitar's range effectively.

patternNote.text: Challenge: Coordinating tapping across different string tensions

notation.title: Tapping Pattern Across All Six Strings

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Adjust tapping pressure for different string tensions - lighter strings need less force. Practice muting adjacent strings to avoid unwanted noise.

exercises.title: Two-Handed Tapping
exercises.description: Use both hands to tap notes on the fretboard simultaneously, creating polyphonic textures and rapid note sequences that showcase the full potential of tapping technique.

patternNote.text: Technique: Independent tapping with both hands

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Start with simple alternating patterns between hands. Each hand should work independently with consistent timing. This creates unique polyphonic textures.

exercises.title: Tapped Arpeggios
exercises.description: Apply tapping to arpeggio patterns to create flowing, extended range chord outlines that cover multiple octaves with smooth legato articulation.

patternNote.text: Harmony: Am - F - C - G arpeggio progression

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Each measure outlines a different chord using tapped high notes and fretted bass notes. This creates beautiful flowing arpeggios with extended range.

exercises.title: Tapped Scale Patterns
exercises.description: Incorporate tapping into scale patterns to create rapid legato runs that extend beyond normal fretboard positions and add unique tonal character to scale passages.

patternNote.text: Scale: A natural minor with tapped extensions

notation.title: A Natural Minor Scale with Tapped Extensions

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: The tapped notes extend the normal scale pattern to higher registers. Practice ascending and descending, maintaining smooth legato throughout the entire passage.

exercises.title: Chromatic Tapping Runs
exercises.description: Create dramatic chromatic passages using tapping to achieve speeds and smoothness impossible with conventional picking techniques. Essential for showcase passages.

patternNote.text: Challenge: Maintaining evenness at high speed

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: This creates dramatic tension through chromatic movement. Use progressive tempo training and focus on maintaining perfect note clarity and evenness.

exercises.title: Multi-String Combinations
exercises.description: Combine multiple advanced tapping techniques across different strings to create complex polyphonic passages that showcase complete mastery of the technique.

patternNote.text: Goal: Independence between multiple tapping voices

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Practice each voice separately first, then combine them. This represents the pinnacle of tapping technique - creating independent melodic lines simultaneously.

items.title: Technical Development
items: Start with basic three-note patterns before advancing
Focus on consistent tapping pressure and timing
Practice muting techniques to avoid unwanted noise
Use a metronome for consistent tempo development
Record yourself to identify timing inconsistencies

challenges.title: Inconsistent Volume
challenges.text: Practice controlling tapping force to match fretted note volumes. Tapped notes often sound louder initially.

challenges.title: String Noise
challenges.text: Use proper muting techniques with both hands. Practice touching only the intended strings cleanly.

challenges.title: Hand Independence
challenges.text: Develop each hand separately before combining. Practice simple patterns to build coordination gradually.
